purpose: Measure the spatial concentration of observed source appearance before evaluating a two-continuous-atom hypothesis. This is an assumption diagnostic, not denoising or a quality score.
input: Authenticated recorded raw_rgb/raw_rgba RGB image aliases; capture metadata and raw SHA preserved as external pins. Inventory all20; exclude six schema1 captures lacking capture-recorded image hashes and matching ROI origin before any measurement. No native outputs, guide values or clean labels.

regions.historical_water_roi: y25:85, x5:85 from the earlier water study, fixed before measurement; spatial location does not prove the same water object in all captures
regions.roi_tiles: four nonoverlapping 30x40 quadrants of that ROI

views: separable Hann with weighted DC subtraction
metrics: Orthonormal full 2D FFT RGB energy, grouped into real conjugate-frequency pairs including self-conjugate bins. Report best shared-RGB integer-pair energy fractions at K=2,8,64, pairs needed for 50% and90%, spatial RMS and top2 frequency coordinates. These are descriptive in-frame fits, not source-noise estimates.
implementation_validation: Parseval/group identity and reconstruction against direct orthogonal projection; exact two-integer-wave, constant, and independently generated off-grid-wave cases. No score-driven parameter changes.
limitations: Historic schema3/4 split and schema5/6 Joint captures are not current alpha captures and not a valid temporal replay
Observed source contains unknown noise; energy concentration does not identify true detail or artifact
Integer-pair concentration can underestimate a continuous off-grid model because of leakage
Hann changes the measured field; it is a leakage sensitivity view, not an estimator output
Low capacity for observed appearance need not imply harm when a signed residual is retained
Separate captures/crops are not camera-aligned and cannot be treated as temporal samples
